Three Dot Punctuation Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Three Dot Punctuation because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+2056, which you can use as ⁖ in HTML, \2056 in CSS, or type with Alt+8278 on Windows (BMP only). If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Three Dot Punctuation is outside both legacy code pages, which is why U+2056 is the identifier that works across Word, HTML, CSS, Python and JavaScript. Three Dot Punctuation has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape ⁖ or the hex escape ⁖.

How to type three dot punctuation on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 8 2 7 8 on the numeric keypad for the decimal codepoint 8278.
  4. Release Alt. The Three Dot Punctuation character (⁖) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type three dot punctuation on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Three Dot Punctuation. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Three Dot Punctuation" and click the character to insert it.

How to use three dot punctuation in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\2056"; ()
  • Python: \u2056 or chr(0x2056)
  • JavaScript: \u2056 or String.fromCodePoint(0x2056)
  • JSON: "\u2056"

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for ⁖?

No legacy Alt code exists for Three Dot Punctuation because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+2056 in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type ⁖ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ⁖, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+8278 not work?

Alt+8278 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Three Dot Punctuation?

The Unicode codepoint for Three Dot Punctuation is U+2056. You can use this value in HTML as ⁖, in CSS as \2056, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ⁖ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+2056, then click it.
